title: Bolthausen–Sznitman ancestry for a fixed-size selected population
decision_reason: Explicit N-BBM conjecture, independent status evidence, precisely declared equilibrium formulation, later-theorem scope checks and separated A30 self-pass passed.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: N standard Brownian particles with binary reproduction at rate one per particle and instantaneous removal of a leftmost particle.
problem_fingerprint.domain: R; offsets anchored at current minimum.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Brownian variance t; independent driving motions and branching clocks.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Initial N-particle offsets have the unique invariant law ψ_N; do not replace it with iid limiting densities.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: N→∞; every fixed sample size k≥2 and T>0.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: There exists one c>0, independent of k,T,N, giving FDD convergence for every fixed sample and window.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: a_N=c(log N)^3; target coalescent each specified r-tuple merges at (r−2)!(b−r)!/(b−1)!.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Partition of a uniform sample without replacement by shared ancestors.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Stationary configuration at each fixed N, then N→∞; finite-dimensional distributions only.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Bolthausen–Sznitman partition process over each finite backward time window.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: No computational restriction; uses proved existence of ψ_N.

statement_source_and_scope_match: JB14 Conjecture 86 includes precisely Model 2 (binary N-BBM). MAI16 and PRT22 independently retain its genealogy question. The draft explicitly formulates its equilibrium regime using BT24 Theorem 1.1, with a finite observation window to avoid an undefined pre-initial history. This is a specified equilibrium form of the standard conjecture, not a verbatim theorem-style quantification in JB14. NB09 supplies FDD/rate conventions. No universal constant-one normalization, all-initial-laws claim or BRW equivalence is asserted.
proposed_statement_text: In the stationary offset regime of standard binary N-BBM, does the genealogy of every fixed uniform sample converge in finite-dimensional distributions to the standard Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent after one common c(log N)^3 time rescaling?
applied_significance: Rigorous ancestry model for an asexual population under strong selection, where position is fitness and population size stays fixed.

second_review.arrangement: Separated adversarial self-pass; no independent agent or human review.
issues_found: Initial observation time cannot be left undefined; ancestral partition must not trace before initialization.
Standard Brownian variance and branch rate fix the population clock; different papers use rate 1/2.
An iid approximation to the limiting density is not the finite-N stationary configuration law.
Search found a superseded 2024 author PDF with a later title/version.
Spatial-profile and position-fluctuation theorems could be mistaken for genealogy results; exponential offspring has different branching.
issues_resolved: Used proved ψ_N and a finite forward/backward window; fixed k,T, then N→∞. Equilibrium specialization is explicitly identified.
Retained an unknown common positive c; no unjustified numerical normalization or moment claim.
Defined ψ_N as the joint configuration law.
Read April 9, 2026 v4, full current genealogy paragraph and displacement Theorem 1.1.
Compared full models and main statements; recorded explicit coupling limitation and Poisson integrability mechanism.
